title: Full Recovery
concept: A six-step way to rebuild after a fight you keep having, or a genuine dent in trust — a real new agreement and a set time to prove it, not just a nicer evening.
whenToUse: Use for a repeated fight, or a clear before/after dent in trust, when a normal Weekly Reset can’t hold the topic. Only when you’ve both agreed to sit down for it — never mid-fight, and not in place of a smaller repair.
steps: Warm up first — soften the mood before anything else. Don’t skip this.
Say what happened — both sides, no interrupting.

Acknowledge the impact — before either of you explains. If one of you caused the breach (infidelity, lying, a broken agreement), only that partner acknowledges impact; the hurt partner is never asked to confess in return.
Explain, if asked — only after the other person has actually taken in the impact.
Ask for one change — name it, and agree by when.
Say it out loud, only if it’s true for both of you — “We made it through this. We’re still here.”

phrases.text: I want a Full Recovery conversation. Can we book it for when we’re both calm?
The agreement I’m asking for is ___, visible by ___.
We made it through this. We’re still here. (only if it’s true for both of you)

working: Booked for Saturday, 4pm, phones in another room. They warm up, both say what happened, and B, who broke the agreement, acknowledges the impact before explaining. One proof item for 14 days, checked weekly. Both mean it when they say they made it through.
notWorking: Bringing this up at midnight, mid-fight, both too wound up, no warm-up first. It becomes one more injury. How and when you have this conversation matters as much as what’s said.
activity: Set aside 60–90 calm minutes. Bring one issue only. Write down the agreement and the check-in date before you leave the room.
warn: Not during active conflict. Calm, agreed, scheduled — never sprung on someone.
note: Deciding not to rebuild, or to end the relationship, is a valid outcome of this protocol, not a failure of it.
